title: Rabbi Yusta bar Shunam
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rabbi Mana’s student—Mana being Rabbi Yonah’s son—and questions him in Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 1:4, at the end of Maaser Sheni 5:1, at the end of Shekalim’s first halakhah, and at the end of Megillah 1:1. He also reports Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin in Tanchuma, Vayetze 4. He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 8:7, at the end of Sheviit 6:2 (Tanchuma, Beshalach 11, instead has Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Shunam; Hyman says it should read as in the Jerusalem Talmud), Challah 4:4, Beitzah 3:6, at the end of Moed Katan 1:2, Sanhedrin 2:3, and Vayikra Rabbah 31:9. Eruvin 1:6 has Rabbi Yuta bar Shuneh, but Hyman regards the citation in Midrash Shmuel 23:19 as correct.

notes.text: The ending abbreviations mean the end of halakhah 1 or 2. Yose/Yusta and Yuta bar Shuneh remain Hyman’s reported variants, with his preferred reading attributed.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 2:3:8 directly names Yusta bar Shunam. Sheviit 6:1:23 has the same name and the returnees’ song at Amanos, against Hyman’s supplied 6:2. The consulted Terumot 1:4 and ordinary Tanchuma Vayetzei 4 did not yield his named locus in these bounded reads; no absence is inferred. Hyman’s Mana discipleship and Yose/Yuta/Shuneh edition comparisons remain his reports. Historical provisional-heading notes remain preserved.
